t: Byblos, on the coast of Lebanon, is one of the oldest continuously inhabited towns in the world.
For over two thousand years it shipped cedar and resin to Egypt, absorbing Egyptian culture and religion.
Its royal inscriptions are among the earliest in the Phoenician alphabet, ancestor of the Greek and Latin scripts.
dyk: The Greeks called papyrus byblos after the city through which they obtained it, and from that word came biblion, book, and ultimately the word Bible.
ev: Byblos ships cedar and resin to the pharaohs of the Old Kingdom
Local rulers receive gifts from the pharaohs Amenemhat III and IV
King Rib-Hadda writes dozens of Amarna letters begging Egypt for help
The Egyptian envoy Wenamun bargains with King Zakar-Baal for cedar
The sarcophagus of King Ahiram is inscribed in the Phoenician alphabet
Byblos pays tribute to Ashurnasirpal II of Assyria
Byblos passes under the Achaemenid Empire
Byblos submits to Alexander the Great and its king joins the siege of Tyre
